prompt:
High-fidelity mobile UI design comp: one portrait phone screen filling the frame.

The app is Squirrel, a personal memory aid. This is its "chores" room, designed as a rail concourse split-flap departure board. Same world as a matte-black flap board in a brushed steel chassis — but this composition gives the next thing a whole panel instead of a list row.

STRUCTURE, top to bottom:
1. A slim brushed steel header rail, tiny wide-tracked uppercase monospace: "SQUIRREL" left, "CHORES" right.
2. THE HERO PANEL, occupying the top two-thirds of the screen: a single enormous departure entry at platform-sign scale. A thin orange (#e66d0d) border frames it. Inside, in order: tiny amber monospace "NEXT · NOW"; then the chore name "WATER THE PLANTS" in gigantic condensed uppercase white paint lettering on matte black flap cells, filling the panel width across two lines, individual flap cell divisions clearly visible; then a thin rule; then tiny cream monospace "EVERY WEEK · LAST DONE A WHILE BACK". A single large amber lamp glows in the panel's top right corner.
3. DIRECTLY BENEATH THE HERO, inside the same framed panel, its own row of three action cells rendered as flaps: the first bright orange (#e66d0d) with near-black uppercase monospace "DID IT"; the other two matte black with cream monospace "HOW OFTEN" and "STOP ASKING".
4. THE SCHEDULE STRIP, the bottom third: four compressed single-line rows in much smaller type, dimmer, each a time in cream monospace and a destination in small condensed uppercase — "14:30 DENTIST", "THU BINS OUT", "— THE BOILER NOISE", "SAT RECYCLING". One of these rows is struck out and rendered in dim red with the status "CANCELLED" at its right.

MATERIALS: matte black flap faces, crisp white paint letters, brushed steel chassis, amber lamps, fine mechanical shadow between flaps.
STRICT PALETTE: #17130d #0c0a07 #241f19 #fffbf3 #fed6a7 #e66d0d #b03a1e.
TYPE: one condensed uppercase sans on the flaps in fixed character cells; tiny wide-tracked uppercase monospace for times, captions, status and actions.
MOOD: a public timetable where one departure is imminent and everything else is waiting its turn. Authoritative, mechanical, unarguable. The grid is strict.
